newsitem.title: BELGIUM: World steel output unchanged in September - IISI.
newsitem.headline: World steel output unchanged in September - IISI.

text.p: World steel production was virtually unchanged in September from a year earlier, but was down 1.4 percent in the first nine months of 1996 compared with the same 1995 period, the International Iron and Steel Institute (IISI) said on Wednesday.
September crude steel output amounted to 60.7 million tonnes in the 66 countries which report to IISI compared with 60.8 million tonnes in September 1995.
In January-September, production fell to 544.1 million tonnes from 552.1 million tonnes, IISI said in a statement.
Despite the underlying trend for growing demand in western Europe, crude steel production at 13.9 million tonnes in September remained below year-earlier figures by 5.8 percent.
Improved mill conditions and political stability were behind production growth of 5.5 percent in Turkey to 1.1 million tonnes in September.
In eastern Europe, however, September production fell 11.8 percent to 2.5 million tonnes.

"Production in Russia and Ukraine is stabilising, bringing the former (Soviet Union's) September production total, at an estimated 6.4 million tonnes, to 4.2 percent above the September 1995 level," IISI said.
But a slowdown in industrial production growth in the United States resulted in a 2.5 percent decrease of crude steel output in September to 7.7 million tonnes.
"This reflects negatively also on the September aggregate output for the North American region which at 10.0 million tonnes remained below last year's level by 0.7 percent," IISI said.
In Asia, September output rose compared with last month, especially in China, up 6.5 percent, and in India, up by 10.1 percent.
For the nine-month 1996 period, production increase appeared the strongest in Asia, IISI said.
However, percentage growth was strongest in Mexico, Taiwan, Argentina and former eastern Germany.
The biggest tonnage decrease was seen in the eastern European region and in Japan.
